overall_reason: The job is checking recent deploys: the header and rows are well grouped, but three saturated status tiles and a gradient chip are the heaviest marks, so ornament leads the order.

score.reason: T-SQUINT reads the three coloured tiles before the row titles and the Deploy button; T-SKELETON and T-LEFT-EDGES pass.

findings.where: status tiles left of the row titles, rows at y=82, 142 and 189, 03-lenses/squint/1440-00.png, 1440px
findings.evidence: The squint render shows three solid blots (a violet tile, an orange disc and a pink tile) and a teal chip in the Deploy button, and they read before the 14px/500 row titles. The sweep's gradient hit (SLP-007) finds a 52-degree gradient on the button chip.
findings.before: Four saturated marks in a three-row card.
findings.after: Use small status marks at the text's weight, and keep colour for the one state that needs attention.
findings.why: When the icons lead, the reader sees colours before knowing which deploy failed.

strengths: The header is one line: "Recent deploys" at 14px/600 on the left and the Deploy button on the right.
Each row keeps its title close to its metadata ("Checkout redesign" at y=82, "main · Maya Chen" at y=102), and the timestamps share one right edge at x=670.
not_investigated: 00-contract.md is absent: no visitor mode, audience or brief overrides; judged as a single product illustration (an app component shown in a frame), with Operate-style rules for the component itself.
T-FIVE-SECOND, T-HEADINGS-READ, T-COMPOSITION-RUN, T-STOCK-ORDER and T-ANATOMY: the artifact is one composition in one 1440x900 tile, not a page with sections, a fold or a visitor job.
